parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The development of stem cells to become neutrophils occurs in several stages. Some of these stages are capable of cell division.

Fig. 6.2 is a summary of neutrophil development. Some details of cellular structure are included.

{{figure:figure-6-2-source.webp}}

All three types of granule indicated in Fig. 6.2 are membrane-bound cell structures containing hydrolytic enzymes. Each type of granule contains a different group of enzymes and other chemicals that enable the neutrophil to carry out its role.
parts.text:
State the location in the body where development and maturation of the neutrophil occurs.

{{figure:reviewed_response_2.png}}

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Primary granules contain proteins known as defensins. These bind to cell surface membranes of bacteria and form very small pores in the membrane.
parts.text:
Suggest how defensins contribute to the role of the neutrophil in killing bacteria.

{{figure:reviewed_response_5.png}}

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.stem: Secondary granules contain lysozyme. This is an enzyme that breaks bonds in peptidoglycan molecules.
parts.text:
Explain how the action of lysozyme will lead to the destruction of the bacterial cell.
